paper_metadata.title: CoTi precipitates: The key to high strength, high conductivity and good softening resistance in Cu-Co-Ti alloy

evidence.quote: A novel Cu-Co-Ti alloy with high strength of 480 MPa, high conductivity of 81% IACS and excellent softening temperature up to 600 ◦C was fabricated via solid solution, cold rolling, and aging treatment.

Solute Co and Ti atoms are enriched and form GP zones after aging at 500 ◦C for 0.5 h, as shown in Fig. 2 b.
The EDS result of point A shows that the atomic ratio of Co and Ti is about 1, illustrating that the dark-contrast precipitates should be CoTi phases (inset Fig. 3 d).
The precipitate possesses a B2 structure, and the interplanar spacing of (100) is measured to be 0.292 nm and (110) to be 0.211 nm.

The EDS analysis of point B (inset Fig. 4 d) shows that the atomic ratio of Co and Ti is about 1, indicating that precipitates in the Cu-Co-Ti alloy aged at 500 ◦C for 24 h should also be the CoTi phases.
According to the statistics of TEM images, the average diameters of the precipitates in the alloy aged 8 h and 24 h are 20 nm and 31 nm, respectively (Fig. 2 e and f).
The IFFT pattern indicates that no misfit dislocation is observed on the Cu/precipitate interface, and the Cu/precipitate interface is highly coherent.
The IFFT pattern (Fig. 4 c) reveals that the interface is incoherent.
Dendritic grains are observed in the as-cast sample.
After solution treatment, the dendritic structure is eliminated and a supersaturated solid solution is formed.
The coarse grains are elongated and show a plate texture after rolling.

property_observations.material_state: aged at 500 °C for 8 h, then held 1 h at 600-625 °C

conditions.test_method: hardness drop to 80% of initial value

evidence.quote: After aging at 600–625 ◦C for 1 h, the hardness of the alloy drops to 136 HV which is 80% of the initial value. Consequently, the softening temperature of the Cu-Co-Ti alloy is higher than 600 ◦C.
Precipitation strengthening is mainly achieved via blocking dislocation motion by CoTi precipitates in the Cu matrix.
For the Cu-Co-Ti alloy under peak aging and over peak aging conditions, the strengthening is dominated by the Orowan mechanism [38].
The dislocation density increases sharply due to the introduction of the cold rolling process, resulting in dislocation strengthening in the Cu-Co-Ti alloy.

Both theoretical calculations and experimental results revealed that the solid solution scattering and precipitation strengthening were the dominant mechanisms that affected the electrical and mechanical properties of the alloy, respectively.
